set.body:
Raised by independent review. Contract gap between Epic 2 and Epic 5.

Verification first: the Epic 2 component law is correct. Checked numerically and analytically at k=8, SPD K, cross-partition q=4:

  K_coh = a a^T / (a^T K^-1 a),  K_cfg = K - K_coh

  - rank(K_coh) = 1, min eig 0 (PSD)
  - min eig K_cfg = -8.6e-16, rank k-1 (PSD)   [proof: K^-1/2 K_cfg K^-1/2 = I - uu^T/||u||^2, u = K^-1/2 a]
  - K_coh + K_cfg - K exactly 0
  - K = D(w), a = w/sum(w): K_coh = w w^T / sum(w), and the effect form matches the current
    first-moment implementation (kernel.R:697-703, work/mass) to 5.6e-16 on the cross-partition case
  - K = Sigma^-1: coherent amplitude is exactly the raw regional mean B a, energy divided by
    a^T Sigma a - i.e. a squared-t. This is the right resolution of the raw-vs-whitened tension.

The gap

The law requires a^T K^-1 a - an action of the INVERSE metric. No epic states this in the operator contract. Epic 5 promises "an on-demand local factor/solve handle" without specifying which direction is solvable.

Why it matters for cost, not just typing

For the main case K = Sigma_hat^-1 the quantity a^T K^-1 a is just a^T Sigma_hat a - a quadratic form against the shrunk residual covariance the learner already has, BEFORE inversion. Cost O(k^2), no factorization.

If Epic 2 is implemented against an apply-K-only handle, the same number is obtained by factorizing and solving: O(k^3) per support per edge. That is an extra k^3 term on top of the one Epic 1 preflight already projects, for a quantity that was free upstream.

Acceptance

- The metric handle contract names both directions: apply_K(v) and quadform_Kinv(a) (or retains Sigma_hat).
- Precision-family recipes short-circuit quadform_Kinv(a) to a^T Sigma_hat a with no factorization.
- Epic 1 cost preflight distinguishes factorization work that is required from work induced by a handle that only exposes apply_K.
- A test asserts the two routes agree and that the short-circuit is taken for precision recipes.
set.title: Coherent normalizer needs K-inverse action; metric handle contract must expose it (Epic 2 / Epic 5 gap)
